title: B2 Writing Quiz 2 — Technology & Social Media

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If we had developed stronger data protection laws, users wouldn't be at risk now.
If we developed stronger data protection laws, users wouldn't be at risk now.
If we had developed stronger data protection laws, users wouldn't have been at risk now.
If we had developed stronger data protection laws, users won't be at risk now.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: If + past perfect (past condition), would + base verb (present result): 'If we had developed..., users wouldn't be at risk now.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Social media addiction will keep rising unless platforms won't change their algorithms.
Social media addiction will keep rising unless platforms change their algorithms.
Social media addiction will keep rising unless that platforms change their algorithms.
Social media addiction will keep rising without platforms change their algorithms.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if...not' and is followed by an affirmative clause: 'unless platforms change their algorithms.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Several new privacy features has been added this year.
Several new privacy features have added this year.
Several new privacy features have been added this year.
Several new privacy features have being added this year.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle: 'have been added this year.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This security flaw should fixed immediately.
This security flaw should being fixed immediately.
This security flaw should be fix immediately.
This security flaw should be fixed immediately.
questions.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle: 'should be fixed immediately.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "Please update your app.")
options: The developer told us to update our app.
The developer told us update our app.
The developer said us to update our app.
The developer told us that update our app.
questions.explanation: Reported commands: tell + object + to + base verb: 'told us to update our app.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "You should use two-factor authentication.")
options: She suggested to use two-factor authentication.
She suggested using two-factor authentication.
She suggested me using two-factor authentication.
She suggested that I using two-factor authentication.
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund or 'that + subject + base verb': 'suggested using two-factor authentication.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The startup which she works for it develops AI tools.
The startup for that she works develops AI tools.
The startup for which she works develops AI tools.
The startup she works for which develops AI tools.
questions.explanation: In formal style, the preposition moves before 'which': 'the startup for which she works.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The app launching last month gained millions of users.
The app launched last month gain millions of users.
The app which launched last month gained millions of users.
The app launched last month gained millions of users.
questions.explanation: A passive meaning reduces 'which was launched' to the past participle alone: 'The app launched last month...'

questions.topic: Modal verbs of past deduction (must have)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The hackers must have exploited a weakness in the system.
The hackers must exploited a weakness in the system.
The hackers must have exploit a weakness in the system.
The hackers must has exploited a weakness in the system.
questions.explanation: Past deduction: must have + past participle: 'must have exploited a weakness.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The company should acted sooner to fix the data breach.
The company should have acted sooner to fix the data breach.
The company should have act sooner to fix the data breach.
The company should has acted sooner to fix the data breach.
questions.explanation: Past regret/criticism: should have + past participle: 'should have acted sooner.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Smartphone usage rose dramatically over the past decade.
Smartphone usage has risen dramatically over the past decade.
Smartphone usage have risen dramatically over the past decade.
Smartphone usage have rose dramatically over the past decade.
questions.explanation: 'Over the past decade' links the past to the present, so present perfect is used: 'has risen dramatically.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: By the time the update was released, most users already deleted the app.
By the time the update had released, most users already deleted the app.
By the time the update was released, most users have already deleted the app.
By the time the update was released, most users had already deleted the app.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: 'most users had already deleted the app.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Tech leaders are meeting next week to discuss AI regulation.
Tech leaders meet next week to discuss AI regulation.
Tech leaders will meeting next week to discuss AI regulation.
Tech leaders are meet next week to discuss AI regulation.
questions.explanation: Present continuous expresses a fixed future arrangement: 'are meeting next week.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He said he will release the update soon.
He said he would release the update soon.
He said he would released the update soon.
He said he would have release the update soon.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' shifts back to 'would': 'he said he would release the update soon.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish social media companies take privacy more seriously.
I wish social media companies have taken privacy more seriously.
I wish social media companies took privacy more seriously.
I wish social media companies would take privacy more seriously as a rule.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past simple expresses regret about a present situation: 'I wish social media companies took privacy more seriously.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish developers warned us earlier about the bug.
I wish developers have warned us earlier about the bug.
I wish developers would have warned us earlier about the bug.
I wish developers had warned us earlier about the bug.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past perfect expresses regret about the past: 'I wish developers had warned us earlier.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We had our website redesigned by a professional agency.
We had redesigned our website by a professional agency.
We had our website redesign by a professional agency.
We have our website redesigned by a professional agency last year.
questions.explanation: Causative form: have + object + past participle shows someone else did the action: 'had our website redesigned.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Never before the industry had faced such rapid change.
Never before had the industry faced such rapid change.
Never before did the industry faced such rapid change.
Never before has the industry had faced such rapid change.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbials at the start trigger inversion: 'Never before had the industry faced...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The company is looking the data leak into.
The company is looking in to the data leak.
The company is looking into the data leak.
The company is looking into to the data leak.
questions.explanation: 'Look into' means 'investigate' and is inseparable: 'looking into the data leak.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: What we urgently need are a clear regulation on AI.
That we urgently need is a clear regulation on AI.
What we urgently need is clear regulation on AI it.
What we urgently need is a clear regulation on AI.
questions.explanation: 'What' clefts take a singular verb when the complement is singular: 'What we need is a clear regulation.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Some apps protect user data well, whereas others sell it to advertisers.
Some apps protect user data well, whereas others sells it to advertisers.
Some apps protect user data well whereas, others sell it to advertisers.
Some apps protect user data well despite others sell it to advertisers.
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two clauses and is followed directly by the subject: 'whereas others sell it...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: In spite the new safeguards, cyberattacks remain common.
In spite of the new safeguards, cyberattacks remain common.
Despite of the new safeguards, cyberattacks remain common.
In spite of the new safeguards, cyberattacks remain common though.
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' is followed by a noun phrase: 'In spite of the new safeguards, cyberattacks remain common.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A number of studies has linked heavy screen time to poor sleep.
The number of studies have linked heavy screen time to poor sleep.
A number of studies have linked heavy screen time to poor sleep.
A great number of studies has linked heavy screen time to poor sleep.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb: 'a number of studies have linked...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She spoke in behalf of the entire developer team.
She spoke on behalf for the entire developer team.
She spoke behalf of the entire developer team.
She spoke on behalf of the entire developer team.
questions.explanation: 'On behalf of' means 'representing someone': 'she spoke on behalf of the team.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The implementation of stricter encryption reduced data breaches significantly.
The implement of stricter encryption reduced data breaches significantly.
The implementing of stricter encryption reduced data breaches significantly.
The implementation of stricter encryption reduce data breaches significantly.
questions.explanation: Formal writing often nominalizes verbs into nouns: 'implement' becomes 'the implementation of...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email requesting information about a software subscription?
options: I'm writing to ask you about your subscription plans, ok?
I am writing to enquire about your subscription plans.
Just wanted to know about your subscription plans.
Hey, tell me about your subscription plans.
questions.explanation: 'I am writing to enquire about...' is a standard formal opening for information requests.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about a delayed software refund?
options: I'm writing because I'm really mad about my delayed refund.
I want to complain about my delayed refund, it's bad.
I am writing to express my concern about my delayed refund.
I am writing to express my concern about my delayed refund, ok.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use measured language such as 'I am writing to express my concern about...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The results of the survey were extreme alarming.
The results of the survey were extremely alarm.
The results of the survey were very much alarming.
The results of the survey were extremely alarming.
questions.explanation: 'Extremely' (adverb) modifies the adjective 'alarming': 'were extremely alarming.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The app is faster now. Moreover, it uses less data.
The app is faster now, moreover it uses less data.
The app is faster now. Moreover it uses less data.
The app is faster now moreover, it uses less data.
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'The app is faster now. Moreover, it uses less data.'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You'd recommend stronger privacy settings, didn't you?
You'd recommend stronger privacy settings, wouldn't you?
You'd recommend stronger privacy settings, would you?
You'd recommend stronger privacy settings, wouldn't it?
questions.explanation: A positive statement with 'would' takes a negative tag: 'You'd recommend..., wouldn't you?'
